Three lower/inset contact-position diagnostics failed and one exceeded the fixed 0.8 N limit; preserve those negative results and do not repeat contact_x/radius changes.
Fresh cases 213002 and 213003 completed qualified; 213000 and 213001 failed with hip/knee contact, so completion remains the first target.

Seed 221001 fails P5 laptop closing before the changed route is used: final angle 1.13489 rad after 32 s, max force 0.65860 N, contact retained but no closure; this is a contact/controller failure, not a route-clearance failure.

P6 is a different controller (0.60 N, 0.30 s on/0.15 s off, 24 s horizon), not merely a lower force cap; it closed 3/4 prior fresh cases but full qualification was 2/4, so it is a hypothesis, not a proven fix.
Near-distance .045 increased alignment 12 to 15 and is rejected; XY terminal deadband regressed and is rejected; 4 mm station tracking timed out and is rejected.
No matched qualified pairs exist for P5 vs P6 or for any new P5 speed change; fresh scenarios will differ.

candidates.predicted_measurement: Laptop reaches release/dwell within the 24 s horizon with no non-hand contacts and max force at or below the global guard, with realized position/force reported; failure to close or higher non-hand contacts rejects it.

candidates.predicted_measurement: Measured closing speed tracks closer to 0.30 rad/s, max force and stall time do not increase versus P5, and closure/dwell improves or remains comparable; no closure or higher force/non-hand contacts rejects it.

P6 full qualification was 2/4, so it is not a validated success.
No matched qualified pairs exist; step/alignment claims are unverified.

analysis: XY terminal deadband regressed on the laptop leg (154 steps/56 alignment vs baseline 110/12), so it is rejected and not reproposed.
The 4 mm station-tracking candidate timed out at 367 alignment steps and is rejected; station pose/tolerance should not be tightened further.

Seed 221000 completed clock/drawer/laptop/recoveries, then right_ankle_roll_link hit laptop-base-contact after the initial laptop-clearance maneuver; root after clearance was (0.309772, 0.107703), with laptop-base-contact AABB x .015-.265, y .085-.255.
213000 failed with left_hip_roll_link vs laptop-contact during release; 213001 failed with right_knee_link vs printer-output-tray-contact during walking; 213002/213003 qualified.
Current commanded closing-speed target is 0.40 rad/s; near-zero measured speed is not the same as demand, and apparent elbow/wrist plateaus are not proven joint-limit causes.

candidates.mechanism: Move the initial laptop-clearance target farther below the laptop-base-contact AABB while keeping x at the permitted maximum, reducing the chance that the right ankle/foot sweeps into the laptop base during the post-laptop departure.
candidates.predicted_measurement: No right_ankle_roll_link/laptop-base-contact during the initial clearance/walk segment on the seed-221000-like case, with unchanged task success and no increase in falls or support-capture failures.

candidates.mechanism: Use the native 12 mm arrival tolerance rather than the rejected 4 mm tracking demand, reducing late alignment corrections without relaxing support capture or heading checks.
candidates.predicted_measurement: Fewer alignment/correction steps and lower alignment count on the laptop leg versus the 4 mm-tracking failure, with realized position error reported and success not worse than baseline.

candidates.mechanism: Start task-alignment earlier on the laptop corridor so heading/lateral corrections happen before the final approach, aiming to reduce late chattering corrections without changing support capture or terminal capture guards.
candidates.predicted_measurement: Lower alignment/correction step count on qualified laptop walking legs, with no increase in falls, support-capture failures, or non-hand contacts; if alignment steps rise or chattering increases, reject.

limitations: Development diagnostics only; fresh scenarios will differ.
No matched qualified pairs exist, so step-reduction claims are unverified.
The ankle/laptop-base collision is observed once; lowering clearance y is a bounded hypothesis, not a proven fix.
Station tolerance and near-distance changes are not isolated from each other; run separately.
No evaluator, physics, force-limit, threshold, or task-order changes are proposed.
